title: 45° Glute Hyperextension
summary: A 45-degree back extension done with a rounded upper back and toes turned out, to make it a glute exercise rather than a lower-back one.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.6 for hamstrings (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.3 for lower back (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Set the pad just below your hip bones, with your toes turned out.
Round your upper back slightly and lower until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips into the pad and squeeze your glutes to come up.

form_cues.cue: Rise until your body is straight
Stop at a straight line. Don't overextend at the top.

mistakes.text: Hyperextending the back at the top.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds no ramp-up sets; make the first working set a touch lighter if you like.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 10-15 reps, stopping about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
